steps.title: Effect on Structure
steps.body: Serialisation required cliffhangers at chapter ends. Each instalment needed a hook to make readers buy the next. This creates episodic, suspenseful pacing.

steps.title: Moral Purpose
steps.body: Victorian novels often had explicit moral messages. Dickens used fiction to campaign for social reform. Literature was seen as a way to educate and improve society.

steps.title: Victorian Values
steps.body: Novels promoted hard work, charity, self-improvement, and Christian morality. Characters who ignore these values face consequences.

steps.title: AO2 Conventions Strategy
steps.body: When analysing a 19th century novel, AO2 (language, form, structure) typically carries 33% of marks. The highest-achieving responses don't just identify conventions — they explain why the writer chose them and what effects they create. Examiners reward analysis of how conventions shape meaning, not labelling of features. For Grade 9, show how writers use, subvert, or combine conventions deliberately to create specific effects on the reader.
